LESSON: READING ALOUD: GRADE APPROPRIATE TEXTS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading 2.5 Guided Reading: Picture Reading (2 sessions) • Picture events • Oral
Topic 2.7: Reading Aloud: Grade Appropriate Texts

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading Aloud: Grade Appropriate Texts. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is reading important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a simple text with appropriate speed for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING ALOUD: GRADE APPROPRIATE TEXTS
This lesson teaches Reading Aloud: Grade Appropriate Texts for Grade 4 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. read a simple text with appropriate speed for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading Aloud: Grade Appropriate Texts using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading Aloud: Grade Appropriate Texts above.
2. Explain Reading Aloud: Grade Appropriate Texts to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading Aloud: Grade Appropriate Texts.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading Aloud: Grade Appropriate Texts with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading Aloud: Grade Appropriate Texts important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is reading important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. read a simple text with appropriate speed for comprehension

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
